display_name: The Immigration Act 2009 (NZ) — eligibility, unlawful status and work, deportation liability and employers — under one top-level goal (for a non-citizen on a day: barred from a visa, unlawful and barred from working, since when, appeal deadline, s 161 liability) and four goals

others: is barred from a visa … on (imm-status.l4)
the day unlawful status starts for (imm-status.l4)
the resident is liable for deportation under s 161 (imm-deportation.l4)
the last day of deportation liability (imm-deportation.l4)
the employer commits an offence under s 350 (imm-employers.l4)

scope: ss 9, 15-17, 21, 154, 157, 161, 167, 185 and 350 of the PCO's version as at 10 July 2026, from the text converted from the PCO XML. The s 179 table of prohibition periods is lost in the conversion and is not encoded.

not_reviewed.note: No domain expert has read this against the Act. An independent test pass was run on 2026-10-16 (tests-independent.l4, 93 assertions from expectations written before the encoding was read); all passed, and the differences it noted are recorded as known limits. The pipeline has not been run. On 2026-10-17, at the user's direction, Legislation Act 2019 s 55 was applied to the deadlines for a humanitarian appeal (s 154), for reconsideration (s 185(2)), for giving reasons against deportation (s 157(2)) and for appealing a deportation liability notice (ss 157(4), 161(2)); 5 independent assertion(s) written before that change now fail by design.

forks.F1: ss 15(1)(b), 350: the anniversary is inside the preceding period.
forks.F2: ss 161(3), 167(2): excluded time extends the period by those days.
forks.F3: 'Not later than N years after' includes the anniversary.
forks.F5: s 9(2)(b): refused without an expiry date.
forks.S55: Legislation Act 2019 s 55 (applied 2026-10-17 at the user's direction): the deadlines for a humanitarian appeal (s 154), for reconsideration (s 185(2)), for giving reasons against deportation (s 157(2)) and for appealing a deportation liability notice (ss 157(4), 161(2)) run to the next working day (Legislation Act s 13, with the Matariki dates in Schedule 1 of the Te Kāhui o Matariki Public Holiday Act 2022) when they end on a non-working day.
